title: What .clone() costs
summary: A clone is a real deep copy - often a hidden allocation used to silence the borrow checker.
lecture: Calling .clone() on a String or Vec allocates fresh heap memory and copies every element. Cloning a Vec<String> clones the vector AND every string inside it. It is never free, and unlike in reference-counted languages it is never just a pointer bump (that's Rc::clone, a different thing).

Clones are legitimate when two owners genuinely must exist independently. The anti-pattern - the one this app trains you to feel - is cloning to make a move error go away. If the callee only reads the value, the correct fix is a borrow; the clone merely hides the design question and pays an allocation to do so.
A useful reflex: every time you type .clone(), ask 'who needs to own this second copy?'. If the answer is 'nobody, I just needed the compiler to stop complaining', it's a borrow in disguise.
